questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: In Economics, decisions are usually taken ‘at the margin’. What does this mean?

options.A: They are concerned with actions that occur in free market not planned economies.
options.B: They are concerned with issues on the boundary between macroeconomics and microeconomics.
options.C: They are concerned with the choice between normative and positive actions.
options.D: They are concerned with the effect of adding a further action to the current level of activity.

options.A: It accounts for only a small proportion of household expenditure.
options.C: Household expenditure on milk will decrease if the price of milk increases.

questions.questionText: When demand for a good falls, its price falls. What is the function of the price fall?

options.A: to eliminate shortages
options.C: to send a signal to producers
options.D: to stimulate a further fall in demand

questions.questionText: When is a rise in the price of a product likely to cause more resources to be allocated to its production?

options.A: if demand increases when the supply curve is perfectly inelastic
options.B: if the demand curve shifts to the right when the supply curve is inelastic
options.C: if supply increases when the demand curve is perfectly inelastic
options.D: if the supply curve shifts to the left when the demand curve is elastic

questions.questionText: A congestion charge of £10 per day has been imposed on motorists taking their cars into Central London. What is it about driving into Central London that provides the economic justification for this charge?

options.A: The external benefits are greater than the external costs.
options.B: The private costs are greater than the external costs.
options.C: The social benefits are greater than the private benefits.
options.D: The social costs are greater than the private costs.

questions.questionText: A government admits that building a new bridge would produce a positive net benefit to society. Owing to a lack of public funds, the bridge would have to be built and operated by a private company, that would charge the public to use the bridge. Private companies insist that building the bridge would not be profitable. What could explain the companies’ unwillingness to build the bridge?

options.A: A private company will be unable to obtain the consumer surplus of the users.
options.B: Building the bridge will give rise to negative externalities.
options.C: The demand for bridge crossings is price-inelastic.

questions.questionText: What is a merit good?

options.A: a good or service which has higher social costs than private costs
options.B: a good or service which has no opportunity cost
options.C: a good or service which is both non-excludable and non-rival
options.D: a good or service which has a greater value than individuals recognise

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, what will happen if a British company raises the sterling (£) price of goods it sells to Pakistan by the full extent of a depreciation of sterling against the Pakistan rupee?

options.A: The demand for the company’s goods will fall in Pakistan.
options.B: The company’s earnings in Pakistan will remain constant in pounds sterling.
options.C: The company’s earnings in Pakistan will remain constant in Pakistan rupees.
options.D: The profit margin on sales to Pakistan will decline.
